> **Required package:** [`Dapper.FluentMap`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Dapper.FluentMap)

## Problem solved

Consult the maintained dependency and runtime compatibility contract.

## When to use it

Use this capability when the column shape and .NET model should remain separated by explicit, reviewable configuration.

## Example

```csharp
public sealed class CustomerMap : EntityMap<Customer>
{
    public CustomerMap()
    {
        Map(x => x.Id).ToColumn("customer_id");
        Map(x => x.Name).ToColumn("customer_name");
    }
}
```

## How it works

FluentMap registers typed metadata and applies it through the matching materialization path. SQL, connections, parameters, and lifecycle remain responsibilities of the application and Dapper.

## Current dependency contract

| Dependency | Supported range | Validated stable baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dapper | `[2.1.89,3.0.0)` | `2.1.89` |
| Dommel | `[3.5.3,4.0.0)` | `3.5.3` |

The Dapper range accepts compatible 2.x versions from the minimum onward; it does not pin exactly 2.1.89. Package metadata and this portal are checked against `eng/compatibility-contract.json`.

## Constraints

:::caution
Initialize before concurrent queries and treat the effective configuration as read-only afterward.
:::
